chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan and 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, both together, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment concerning a man who was found killed and it was not known who had killed him. He said: “If he is identified and he has heirs who seek his blood-money, they are to be given his blood-money from the Bayt al-Mal of the Muslims, and the blood of a Muslim man is not to be left without recompense; because his inheritance belongs to the Imam, so likewise his blood-money is upon the Imam. And they pray over him and bury him.”
He said: “And he gave judgment concerning a man whom the people crushed on Friday in the crowding of the people, and he died, that his blood-money is from the Bayt al-Mal of the Muslims.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ: the heirs or legal claimants entitled to seek the diyah
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam as the legitimate authority responsible in such cases
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims from which compensation is paid
key_terms.دِيَتَهُ: his blood-money due as legal compensation for wrongful death
key_terms.مِيرَاثَهُ: his inheritance, mentioned as belonging to the Imam
key_terms.يُصَلُّونَ عَلَيْهِ: they perform the funeral prayer over him

ai.seo_question: Who pays the diyah in Shia fiqh when a murdered person’s killer is unknown or someone dies in a crowd?
ai.summary: This hadith records legal rulings from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding a slain person whose killer is unknown and a person who dies in a crowd on Friday. In both cases, the diyah is paid from the Bayt al-Mal of the Muslims, affirming that the blood of a Muslim is not to be neglected and that public authority bears responsibility where no identifiable individual liability can be established.
